title: Quantization kernel benchmarks (INT8 / FP8 / GPTQ / AWQ) - exploratory notes
body:
Summary:
This exploratory note captures kernel-level benchmarks and quality checks for INT8, FP8, GPTQ, and AWQ quantization paths across toy 7B and 13B decoder models and a small encoder-decoder baseline. Goal: identify kernel bottlenecks, quantify latency/throughput gains, and surface quality regressions on small eval suites.

Setup:
- Hardware: A100-80GB primary; H100 used for FP8 native runs.
- Runtime: serving-runtime dev (commit abc1234), kernel set v0.6-explore.
- Models: openweights-toy-7b, openweights-toy-13b, small 220M encoder-decoder.
- Quant methods: INT8 (sym/asym), GPTQ (per-channel), AWQ (blockwise 64/128), FP8 (E4M3, E5M2).
- Kernels tested: cuBLAS fallback, fused-attn (fp16), fast-igemm-v2 (int8), awq-dequant-fast, fp8-kernel-prototype (emu and native).
- Workloads: streaming token (batch=1 seq 1..2048), batched gen (batch=8 seq=256), embeddings (batch=64).
- Metrics: p95 token latency, median throughput (tokens/sec), GPU peak mem, WikiText perplexity subset, small MMLU probe, Rouge-L on short summaries.

Key findings:
1) INT8 (fast-igemm-v2): ~1.6x speedup vs fp16 on batched 7B; p95 token latency down ~35% for streaming with fused-attn + int8-gemm. Throughput +55%, GPU mem ~30% lower. Quality: ppl +0.8, MMLU -1.4. Small-matrix tiling overhead for seq<16; hybrid fallback to fp16 recommended.

2) GPTQ: similar perf to INT8, slightly better quality (ppl +0.4). Throughput +50% on 13B when using blockwise dequant cache. Quality: MMLU -0.8. Dequantization cost amortized across heads; increases memory traffic.

3) AWQ: strong for CPU and smaller GPUs; on GPU AWQ + fast-dequant ~1.7x vs fp16 for batched 7B with higher variance on streaming. Quality: ppl +0.6, MMLU -0.9. Blocksize tradeoff: 64 better accuracy, 128 slightly faster. Missing tiny-head fusion in kernel (issue filed).

4) FP8: native H100 runs show ~1.9x speedup vs fp16 in batched workloads with minimal quality regression (ppl +0.2). On A100 via emulation gains are minor (~1.1x) and unstable. Need careful scaling to avoid NaNs.

Profiling and bottlenecks:
- Dequant + reorder is the largest overhead for GPTQ/AWQ in short-sequence workloads. Remedies: fuse dequant+GEMM, cache dequantized blocks, lazy dequant for hot KV slices.
- Small-matrix inefficiency for int kernels (tiling overhead). Hybrid router to send small mats to fp16 helps.
- Kernel memory traffic: per-block scales increase reads; measure PCIe impact for host-resident weights.
- Attention fusion: fused-attn optimized for fp16; need equivalent fused paths for int/awq/fp8 to reduce copies.

Quality summary:
- INT8: large speedups, modest quality drop; acceptable for non-SLA-sensitive cases.
- GPTQ: balance of speed and quality; good default for Dedicated for 13B+.
- AWQ: promising accuracy-preserving int approach; needs blocksize tuning.
- FP8: best when HW-native; emulation not competitive.

Recommendations:
- Implement fused dequant+GEMM kernels for GPTQ/AWQ (high priority).
- Add hybrid kernel router: route short-seq to fp16 fused path, long-seq to int/gptq/awq fast paths (medium).
- Add dequantized-block caching in KV pipeline with eviction policy tied to traffic (medium).
- Expand eval to 1k prompts with hallucination and factuality probes before production rollouts (high).
- Add FP8 native testing on H100 in CI; disable FP8 emulation on A100 by default (low->medium).

Quick numbers (7B, batch=8, seq=256, A100):
- fp16 baseline: throughput 12.1k t/s, p95 7.4ms, GPU mem 46GB, WikiText ppl 13.2
- INT8: throughput 18.7k t/s, p95 4.8ms, mem 32GB, ppl 13.9
- GPTQ: throughput 18.2k t/s, p95 5.0ms, mem 34GB, ppl 13.6
- AWQ (b=64): throughput 17.9k t/s, p95 5.2ms, mem 33GB, ppl 13.8
- FP8 (A100 emu): throughput 13.4k t/s, p95 6.6ms, mem 31GB, ppl 13.4

Open items / next steps:
- Re-run full 2k-prompt suite per quant scheme and produce per-prompt delta distributions.
- Implement fused dequant+gemm prototype (Arjun).
- Empirically find hybrid router thresholds (Maya).
- Add per-token cost estimates for each scheme to quantify unit economics.
- Fix AWQ tiny-head fusion and rebench blocksize tradeoffs (Evan).

Provenance and artifacts:
- Bench harness: github:repo/benchmarks (script bench/quant_kernels_v0.sh)
- Runtime commit: abc1234 (serving-runtime dev)
- Creator: Riley Chen (eng-serving-runtime)

This doc is a working exploratory note. Numbers are approximate and captured in the bench harness for reproducibility. Next step: convert into a structured bench report with CSV outputs and plots when fused-kernel prototype is available.
